correctness.rationale: Exact small-vertex exposure and disjoint triangle clipping prove the formula; derivative and Taylor expansion prove strict extrema and sharp onset, and circular-arc intersection monotonicity plus polar slicing prove weighted extension. All boundary cases n>=3, b<=a, tangency and equal scales accounted for. A literal independent vertex-clipper checked 7200 samples, with no reliance on a finite test for universal proof.

originality.rationale: Material comparisons against Mathar (concentric containment), Kiss–Vidnyánszky (congruent regular union), Har-Peled–Roy (translation overlap), and two full published published-finding corpus proofs (congruent radial union, random expected overlap) did not find the fully quantified unequal-scale area profile, strict phase regime and quadratic-to-linear contact transition. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Generic clipped-regular-polygon formulas may have appeared in older geometric overlap literature under different terminology.
Some unindexed or inaccessible results could contain the same all-scale area law.
The containment threshold and equal-scale radial arc methods are prior art, not separate new results.

value.rationale: Scale mismatch and rotational registration form a natural shape-comparison problem. The theorem completely classifies all phases and scale ratios, exposes a sharp no-loss plateau, an optimal half-step mismatch, a qualitative contact-order transition and dominance for every radial density. This is a structural geometric phase diagram rather than an unmotivated numerical special case.
